key_idea: Just run the constraint propagation the statement describes to a fixpoint: any triple (cell, two cells below) with two known values determines the third.
sketch: Repeat passes over all triples v[i][j] = v[i+1][j] + v[i+1][j+1]; when exactly two are known fill the third, and when all three are known check consistency. A derived value outside [-99,99] or an inconsistent triple gives 'no solution'; unknown cells left at the fixpoint give 'ambiguous'; otherwise print the pyramid. At most 5050 cells so repeated passes are cheap (each pass fills at least one cell). Order of checks matters: a contradiction or out-of-range value wins over unfilled cells. Caveat: 'ambiguous' is taken in the statement's sense (propagation cannot finish), not full linear algebra; a card like top and two bottom corners known for n=3 is linearly determined but reported ambiguous here.
